text: Meridian Fabrication is standing up WIN-SRV-04, a new file and print server about to hold production data for the shop floor. Before it goes live, it has to pass the same hardening checklist every server in this domain gets, and that checklist is just the first three chapters of this course, applied in order, end to end, on one real machine.

First, the CIS-based GPO baseline from Chapter 2: joining the Servers OU applies disabled SMBv1, a strong password policy, and LAPS-managed local admin credentials. Gpupdate forces it, gpresult proves which policies actually landed, and a GPO report goes in the change ticket as evidence the server left staging compliant.

Windows Firewall has three profiles, and this server only ever talks to the network as a domain member. The Domain profile allows SMB and RDP, but only from the management subnet, never from Any. Private and Public stay at default deny-all-inbound, because this server will never legitimately sit on either network type.

BitLocker encrypts the drive, but the step teams skip is backing up the recovery key to Active Directory instead of a sticky note, so a crashed disk doesn't mean a lost key an admin can never retrieve. Audit policy gets set subcategory by subcategory, logon, group management, security state change, instead of the old blunt legacy categories that flood the log with noise nobody reads.

Native Windows logging stops at knowing a process ran. Sysmon fills that gap: installed with a baseline ruleset, it turns on process creation, network connection, and file creation logging, written to its own operational log. Confirming those events are flowing is the last check before this server counts as production-ready.

Every one of those five steps traced straight back to a chapter this course already covered — none of this was new material, just that material applied under real pressure. Next up, the same checklist runs again on the other operating system in this environment: hardening a Linux server baseline, from sudoers to SSH to the auditing rules that watch it all.
